fdroid:com.al.countforme.name: Count for me
fdroid:com.al.countforme.summary: An interval timer you write, not one you just set.
fdroid:com.al.countforme.description:
An opinionated interval timer built for workouts that do not fit neatly into standard work, rest, and round patterns.
 What it does 
 Timers that announce and stop. A single cue when the timer reaches zero, like a sports watch, with no alarm to dismiss.
 Two interval modes that fit how you think. Build workouts from work, rest, cycles, and sets, or define a block, cycle, and work duration and let the timer calculate the rest and cycle count.
 Variable cadence timer. Split a block into ranges and give each range its own rate. Repeat the complete pattern across rounds.
 Themes that carry their sound and their music. A theme is the colours, the sound of every cue, the spoken counts, and the music the workout runs to, in one folder. The app ships with one; make your own from blank or from a copy, edit it in place, and see it live.
 Music the cues cut through. Play your own music in the app and every cue ducks it: the song drops as the cue lands and comes back between, by however much and however fast you set.
 Presets in categories. Save a complete setup by name, group presets into categories, and pick one back up from the top of the screen. A category can name a theme, and picking a preset from it puts that theme on — its look, its cues, and its music, or as much of that as the category asks for.
 Presets and themes that travel. Export what a tab holds to a file, or a theme as a zip, and hand it to someone else. Import either from anywhere on the phone.
 What it can become for you 
Nothing above is new in kind. It is deeper. A theme is not colours any more but colours, sounds and music. A preset is not alone but in a category, and a category can carry a theme. Both travel.
Put those together and you are not saving a workout. You are saving a story line.
A set of workouts with its own palette, its own gong, its own voice counting the reps, its own music underneath it all, and names that mean something to you, is an identity. Someone who opens it does not open five squats, five push-ups, five pull-ups, five rounds. They open a room you made, and the workout is what happens in it. A program can walk them through levels of it, each with its own look and sound.
This is a tool for creators and for a community. It is made for sharing your programs and what stands behind them: the part of you that does not usually travel with a program. Your mood, your thinking, the zone you are in. Sounds, colours, themed categories, the names of the workouts and the workouts themselves all say it, and they say it together.
You are the creator, and you decide what this app is. Another interval timer, or far more than that. It is in your hands.

fdroid:com.lord1egypt.pocketclaw.name: PocketClaw
fdroid:com.lord1egypt.pocketclaw.summary: A private AI agent that runs on your Android phone, with real on-device tools
fdroid:com.lord1egypt.pocketclaw.description:
PocketClaw is a private AI agent that runs on your Android phone. The language model is remote — you bring an API key for the provider you choose — but everything else lives on the device: the agent's gateway, its tools, its workspace and your credentials.
 What it does 
 An on-device agent gateway, bound to loopback only. The background core uses about 20 MB of memory (PSS) while idle and roughly 26–33 MB during active agent work on our Android 16 test phone; the app's screens and web view use more while they are open.
 A Managed Runtime of real command-line tools compiled for the phone and shipped inside the APK: python 3.14, git 2.51, gh 2.101, curl 8.11, ripgrep 14.1, sqlite3 3.50 and jq 1.7. PocketClaw never downloads its runtime after install; the tools reach the network only when the agent uses them for something you asked.
 Skills: reusable instruction and tool bundles. The agent can find and install them from the ClawHub registry or GitHub when you ask it to.
 A local web dashboard for providers, models, channels, skills and logs, in 14 languages. It opens inside the app, and in a browser on your own network if you turn on Public Mode.
 Chat with the agent in the app, or over Telegram.
 A workspace directory in the app's own storage that the agent reads and writes.
 The app itself in 12 languages, right-to-left included.
 Requirements 
 An arm64-v8a device with Android 8.0 or newer. The bundled tools and the agent runtime exist for arm64 only.
 An API key for a model provider, or an OpenAI-compatible endpoint you run yourself.
 Network services 
PocketClaw contacts nothing until you configure it. It then talks only to what you set up:
 The model provider you choose. Built-in templates include proprietary services (Anthropic, OpenAI, Google Gemini, AWS Bedrock, Azure OpenAI and others) and self-hosted ones (Ollama, vLLM, any OpenAI-compatible server).
 Telegram, if you connect it. One-tap setup uses PocketClaw's onboarding service, whose source is published under the MIT licence; a manual bot token works without it.
 Whatever the agent's tools reach when you ask them to: web search (Sogou by default; SearXNG and others are selectable), git remotes, GitHub, the ClawHub skill registry, URLs you give it.
There are no analytics, no crash reporting and no update checks.
 Anti-feature: non-free network services 
PocketClaw promotes and integrates with proprietary network services: hosted AI model providers, Telegram and other chat platforms, web search and the ClawHub skill registry. None of them is required — a self-hosted OpenAI-compatible model server and the in-app chat are enough.
PocketClaw's own code is MIT licensed. The agent core is based on PicoClaw.

fdroid:com.pebblentn.app.name: PebbleNTN
fdroid:com.pebblentn.app.summary: Turn-by-turn directions from your phone's nav apps on your Pebble watch
fdroid:com.pebblentn.app.description:
PebbleNTN — Pebble Notification To Navigation — puts the turn-by-turn directions from your phone's navigation app onto your Pebble watch, so you don't have to reach for your phone while you ride, walk or drive.
It works by reading your navigation app's notifications on the phone and sending the next step to the watch: distance, road name, and — depending on the app — the maneuver arrow and ETA. Nothing is sent to any server — the notification is parsed on your device and forwarded to your paired Pebble over the local connection.
Supported navigation apps:
* Google Maps (English plus German, French, Spanish, Italian and Dutch) — maneuver arrow, distance, road and ETA
* Organic Maps — distance and road; the watch shows a neutral turn marker (no ETA)
* CoMaps — distance and road; the watch shows a neutral turn marker (no ETA)
* OsmAnd — distance and road; the watch shows a neutral turn marker (no ETA)
Full maneuver arrows and ETA for these apps depend on data they don't currently put in the notification text; support may improve in a future update.
PebbleNTN recognises each app's notifications with a small, declarative rule set that ships with the app, so support for more apps can come in future releases. You can write your own rules for an unsupported app, or share an anonymised capture log to help add official support.
Features:
* Next maneuver, distance, road and ETA on the watch (maneuver icon and ETA are currently Google Maps only — see supported apps above)
* Automatic watchapp launch when navigation starts (configurable in settings)
* Three arrow styles, accent colours, and light or dark themes
* Metric or imperial units, left- or right-hand arrow layout
* Privacy-first: the notification is parsed locally and never uploaded; the optional "share logs to help" step lets you review and redact before sharing
* No ads, no tracking, no account
Permissions:
* Notification access — to read the navigation app's turn-by-turn notification (this is the core function)
* Internet — not used on Google Play installs, which get their updates from Google Play. Installs from GitHub, F-Droid or Obtainium use it only for an optional check for a newer version on GitHub (when you tap Check for updates, or weekly if you turn it on); it sends no personal data
Requires a paired Pebble watch and the Pebble/Rebble companion app installed on the phone. The matching Pebble watchapp is distributed separately (Rebble app store / .pbw).

fdroid:io.paperterm.app.name: PaperTerm
fdroid:io.paperterm.app.summary: An e-ink-friendly SSH terminal for Android
fdroid:io.paperterm.app.description:
PaperTerm is an SSH terminal built for e-paper devices such as the Onyx Boox range, where
screens redraw slowly and leave ghosting behind. It pairs the Termux terminal engine with a
pure-Java SSH client, and adds the details that make a terminal usable on e-ink.
It is a pure SSH client: there is no local shell and no local code execution.
 Readable on e-paper 
A dark-on-white ANSI palette keeps nvim, less and top legible instead of washing them out.
Ghosting was stress-tested with fast streaming output, large dumps, full-screen inversion,
repeated clears and TUI scrolling: the device's own EPD handling turned out to beat app-level
refresh calls, which caused keyboard flashing, so PaperTerm deliberately stays out of the way.
 Page turning, e-reader style 
Turn pages with the volume keys or on-screen triangles. Auto, Page-keys and Wheel modes let
editors and terminal multiplexers each behave the way they should.
 Korean and CJK input 
Composed syllables appear as they are finalized, without sending backspaces, so vim and other
full-screen apps stay safe. Latin text is sent immediately. Jamo can optionally be shown while
composing.
 A keyboard row you control 
The extra-keys row is fully customizable: a comma separates keys, a semicolon starts a new row,
and KEY=label sets the icon. Any other token is typed literally, so symbols or whole words can

Clench is a Bitcoin-only, non-custodial Bitcoin wallet for Android. It uses Bitcoin Dev Kit and stores wallet data locally on the device.
Wallet features:
- Create single-sig and multisig wallets.
- Import watch-only wallets from descriptors.
- Create or restore BIP-39 seed phrase wallets with an optional passphrase.
- Use native SegWit, nested SegWit, legacy, and Taproot script types.
- Connect to Electrum servers, including personal servers and Tor SOCKS5 routes.
- Use coin control, UTXO freezing, labels, batch payments, RBF fee bumping, CPFP, cancel replacement attempts, raw transaction import, and sweep flows.
- Run node diagnostics for Electrum route, Tor mode, TLS pinning, server version, and tip height.
Hardware-wallet features:
- Exchange PSBTs by animated QR, BBQr, an intentional NFC tap, microSD/user-selected file import, or signed-return import where supported.
- Clench does not communicate with signing devices over USB or Bluetooth. A signer may still use USB for power.
- Work with QR-based signers such as SeedSigner, Keystone, Foundation Passport, and Blockstream Jade. v0.3.28 adds physically unverified protocol presets intended for OneKey Pro, Krux, and Specter DIY; the Krux and Specter DIY presets also include user-selected microSD/file transfer.
- Work with Coldcard Q, Coldcard Mk4, and Coldcard Mk5 transfer paths.
- Check TAPSIGNER NFC Tap Protocol status.
- Sweep SATSCARD active slots with certificate verification and explicit CVC-authenticated unseal confirmation.
- Set up, verify, import, and back up TAPSIGNER cards, and directly sign supported single-signature BIP84 native-SegWit or standard BIP48 native-P2WSH multisig inputs with complete in-app review and returned-signature verification.
- TAPSIGNER payment signing does not support Taproot, legacy, nested SegWit, nonstandard P2WSH, other account paths, or PIN change.
- The OneKey Pro, Krux, Specter DIY, and TAPSIGNER multisig paths have automated coverage but no recorded physical-device acceptance; no model/firmware compatibility claim is made for those new paths.
- Require explicit broadcast confirmation after hardware-wallet signing.
Security and privacy features:
- Encrypt keys with Android Keystore.
- Encrypt the Room application database with SQLCipher. BDK public wallet-state files rely on the Android app sandbox and device encryption.
- Protect wallet access with PIN and biometric authentication where available.
- Validate signed PSBTs and finalized transactions before broadcast.
- Avoid analytics, advertising SDKs, Firebase, Google Play Services, crash reporting services, and account sign-in.
Network use is limited to wallet sync and optional user-triggered fee or price data lookups.

firefox-addons:780964.summary: Easily block all images and videos within a website!
firefox-addons:780964.description:
Block Image|Video is an addon that lets you easily block or hide desired items (image, video, etc.) with just one click. 
Once you add this addon to your Firefox, a button will appear in the toolbar. This button shows that the addon is active (with a red color). Now, before using the addon, please visit the options page and choose a desired item(s) to block or hide (i.e. image). 
By default, NO item is selected. Please note that, if you choose to - hide - items, the addon lets these items to be loaded in the browser, but, will make them invisible. On the other hand, if you choose to – block - any item, the addon prevents that specific item from loading into your browser. This way, loading the web-pages may become faster but you cannot make images to become visible again (if the addon is turned off).
 Note 1 : before using the addon, please visit the options page and adjust the item(s) you want to block or hide.
 Note 2 : to report bugs, please visit the addon homepage and fill the bug report form.

firefox-addons:784025.name: YouTube Dark Theme
firefox-addons:784025.summary: A highly customizable dark charcoal/blue theme for YouTube
firefox-addons:784025.description:
"Dark Theme for YouTube" extension converts YouTube theme to a highly customizable dark charcoal/blue theme. This extension is built on top of the default YouTube theme (native dark theme) so it is very light-weighted compare to using themes injected by Stylish or Stylus extensions.
Extension Preview:
 https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=3lan4mQKxBk 
Features:
Turn on and off from the action button to switch between light and dark themes
Accepts scheduling to turn on only on the specified period
Customize default color scheme
Inject custom CSS to alter the default theme (change font-size or font-family for instance)
How does this extension work?
This extension alters a cookie globally to turn the dark theme on and off. It also injects a lite script to the YouTube pages to alter the color scheme of the root element. In oppose to the other similar extensions, there is no resetting of the default theme or inverting the white theme with an inversion filter. Both of these methods are computationally inefficient. Instead, this extension asks YouTube to turn the native dark theme and only alter the global CSS variables to alter the colors.
Note that this method only works if the product supports native coloring. Some Google products do not yet support this feature.
Privacy Policy: 
This extension does not send or receive any data to any server whatsoever.
Bug Report:
Please either use the commenting section of the FAQs page or the GitHub page for bug reporting.
Change Log:

Use the built-in dark theme (Material Design only)

apple-macos:6792591069.name: Orbit Dashboard
apple-macos:6792591069.description:
Orbit brings your whole life onto one dashboard.
Instead of hopping between ten apps to see what matters, Orbit overlays your calendar, reminders, health, weather, people, money, and more onto a single Today screen — then surfaces what actually needs you.
ONE DASHBOARD, EVERY HORIZON
Switch between Today, This Week, This Month, and This Year to see what's coming — an appointment weeks out, a bill due, a birthday — across every area at once.
CAPTURE ANYTHING, INSTANTLY
One box. Type or dictate, and Orbit's on-device AI files it as a task, note, idea, quote, or person. No folders, no friction.
ASK ORBIT
A private, on-device assistant that answers from your own data, plus a daily summary of your day.
ORBIT NOTICED
Insights that connect two parts of your life no single app sees — a birthday during a busy week, poor sleep before a demanding day, a bill due while you're traveling.
EVERYTHING IN ONE PLACE
• Calendar & Reminders — your events and lists, with inline complete
• Health — activity rings, steps, heart rate, and sleep
• Weather — current conditions, forecast, and threshold alerts
• People — birthdays, important dates, and who to reconnect with
• Money — App Store sales, a stock watchlist, a retirement forecast, and bills
• Projects, Content, Travel, Garage, Journal, Library, Email, Deliveries, and more
WIDGETS EVERYWHERE
One configurable Orbit widget in every size — Home Screen and Lock Screen. Pick what it shows, check off reminders and routines without opening the app, and it follows your theme in Light and Dark.
WORKS WITH APPLE
Siri, Shortcuts, Spotlight, Handoff, and interactive widgets — no setup. Just say "Hey Siri, capture in Orbit."
BUILT FOR EVERY DEVICE
iPhone, iPad, Mac, Apple Watch, and Apple TV, synced over your private iCloud.
PRIVATE BY DESIGN
There's no Orbit account and no Orbit server. What you create stays on your device and in your private iCloud. Capture cleanup and Ask Orbit run on-device with Apple Intelligence. Only a coarse location ever leaves your device — and only to fetch the weather.
Available in English and Spanish.

Privacy Policy: https://ericrogerstechnology.com/Orbit/PRIVACY.html

AutoNote - Private AI Note Taker
Record, transcribe, summarize, and translate with private, on-device AI. Turn audio, video, PDFs, and images into organized, searchable notes. 
AutoNote is your all-in-one AI note-taking assistant, designed with privacy at its core. Whether you're recording a meeting, capturing a lecture, importing a video, reading a PDF, or extracting information from photos and images, AutoNote helps you turn information into useful notes. Forget manual note-taking. Capture information from different sources, get AI-powered summaries, and find what matters - all in one place.
Features for Peak Productivity:
• Privacy-First Design: Your recordings, transcripts, notes, images, and AI chats are processed privately on your device. No AutoNote account required.
